einzeiler: Neuroscientist Rick Hanson explains how neuroplasticity and mindfulness can improve…
kurzfassung: Psychologist Rick Hanson discusses the neuroscience of happiness and how individuals can train their brains for resilience. He explains the concept of neurodharma, combining brain science with contemplative wisdom to overcome mental patterns. Additionally, he shares practical strategies like the five-minute challenge to foster personal growth.
stichpunkte: Rick Hanson realized at age 15 that learning is the ultimate superpower for personal development.
Buddhism and neuroscience share core observations about the constant change and interconnectedness of the mind.
Neurodharma combines subjective internal experiences with objective neuroscience to understand mental reactions.
The negativity bias causes the brain to act like Velcro for bad experiences and Teflon for good ones.
Simple somatic practices like breathing into the insula and looking at the horizon can instantly interrupt monkey mind.
Meditation and mindfulness create structural brain changes in prefrontal regions and regulate emotional responses.
Add-on suffering refers to the mental friction and reactivity that people unnecessarily add to unavoidable life events.
The seven ways of being—steadiness, lovingness, fullness, wholeness, nowness, allness, and timelessness—map the mountain of human potential.
beschreibung:
Dr. Rick Hanson proves the power of positive neuroplasticity in his own journey from a teenager with an anxious mindset and deep unhappiness to an expert on positive brain change and resilience. Wanting to understand why people suffer needlessly led him to study psychology, neuroscience, and Buddhist wisdom, where he discovered that the brain can be trained through small daily practices. In this episode, Rick shares how entrepreneurs can use mindfulness and neuroplasticity to quiet mental noise, reduce unnecessary suffering, build resilience, and stay grounded when business and life get intense.

In this episode, Hala and Rick will discuss:

Rick Hanson is a psychologist, Senior Fellow at UC Berkeley’s Greater Good Science Center, and founder of the Wellspring Institute for Neuroscience and Contemplative Wisdom. He is a New York Times bestselling author of multiple books, including Neurodharma, Buddha’s Brain, and Hardwiring Happiness. Rick also co-hosts the Being Well Podcast with his son, Forrest Hanson, which has been downloaded more than 25 million times.
